research_concepts: counter strategy best and avoid pairings
methodological_questions: Is a player's top sequential suppressor stable across seasons (split-half or season-to-season reliability)?
Do teammate X->Y sequences show large negative premiums after accounting for sample size and regression to the mean?
What sample size per player-season-opponent is needed to estimate suppression premiums reliably?
How should selection of the top suppressor be corrected for regression to the mean and multiple comparisons?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether the engine's top recommended play type beat the team's modal play type in a playoff series. Full-calibrated headline 69.8% (37/53); clean comparisons 64.1% (25/39); no bootstrap CI computed. The record classifies the apparent effect as an artifact (C_artifact) with leakage and small-sample risks. Not a suppression-stability test, but it shows that headline hit rates from this kind of recommendation design were produced by construction and selection flaws.

Possession-level test of a matchup-conditioned play-type picker across regular-season games (n=16,921 cells). Reported positive premiums (e.g., C +0.0714 PPP, p<10^-4) but proxy agreement with the production engine was 16.5% (recorded as below 70%); the record notes in-sample contamination of regular-season aggregates and iid standard errors. Verdict inconclusive, mechanism unclear.

Three-level counter ranking (population, team, matchup). The population-level best counter differed from the team-level best counter for at least one play type (record text truncated at 'L2 best=PNR n'); cells had n_mu from 5 to 696 and playoff matchups from 4 to 44. The record states no validation was recorded. Verdict inconclusive.

Single-game agent demo (MIA vs BOS 2023 G7, 75 MIA possessions) for recovering a conditional decision tree. Most tree cells had n=3-10, and the record states the branches are hypotheses until validated across series. Verdict untestable with that design.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Evaluating a recommended play type against the team's modal play type as a decision-quality test.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact (C_artifact): the apparent effect came from a construction, selection or labelling flaw, with leakage and sample-size risks. No bootstrap CI was computed on n=53.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Regular-season possession-level proxy test of a matchup-conditioned picker.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive (E_unclear). Proxy fidelity was 16.5%, in-sample contamination was present, and standard errors assumed independence.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Checking whether the best counter is stable across population, team and matchup levels.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive (E_unclear). Small matchup cells (n_mu 5 to 696; 4 to 44 playoff matchups) and no recorded validation; the record's own recommendation is that a league default should not be used if the levels disagree.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Recovering conditional sequential decision branches from one game.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable (A_unanswerable): cells of n=3-10 and a single game; branches are hypotheses until validated across series.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on sequential counter and play-type recommendations produced headline effects that were labelled artifacts or inconclusive, mainly from leakage, in-sample contamination, small cells and unvalidated selection.
Matchup-level cells of the sizes used in this project (roughly n=3 to 44) were judged too small to support firm conclusions in the retrieved records.
Top-choice recommendations evaluated on the same data used to select them were a recurring failure pattern.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether any individual's top sequential suppressor is stable across seasons. No retrieved record tests suppressor-identity stability or season-to-season reliability.
Whether teammate X->Y premiums are large or negative after regression to the mean. No retrieved record estimates these premiums with shrinkage or a null distribution.
Any reliability estimate for player-season-opponent suppression premiums at n=20.
The content of the related family FAM:SF-APPS-004, which was mentioned but not returned, and the truncated text of FAM:SF-APPM-055.
own_inferences: Choosing the top suppressor per star from many opponents and teammates by maximum estimated premium will mechanically inflate the chosen premium (RTM), so an observed stable top suppressor could partly reflect noise re-selected each season.

With n=20 per player-season-opponent and many candidate defenders, most cell estimates will be dominated by sampling noise, so stability will be hard to distinguish from chance without a permutation or null baseline.
Multi-season data (2022-23 to 2025-26) allows a split-season reliability test, which the earlier records did not use as a stability test.
Roster and role changes across seasons (DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY) and opponent and teammate usage (CONFOUNDING) are likely to affect any premium estimate.
uncertainties: The retrieval returned no record directly on suppressor stability or teammate X->Y premiums, so the relevance of prior work is partial.
The stated unit size n=20 is ambiguous: it is unclear whether it refers to possessions, games, or matchups per cell.
Whether the 2025-26 season files, which are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, will be complete at analysis time.
No follow-up tool was called to read the full text of the truncated records.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that earlier counter and play-type recommendation tests in this project were repeatedly labelled artifact, inconclusive or untestable, mainly from leakage, in-sample contamination, small cells and unvalidated selection. This pushed the decision away from a direct test of the top-suppressor claim and towards a reliability-first design with out-of-sample selection and shrinkage, and against using best or avoid recommendations until reliability is shown.

blocking_constraints.text: n=20 per player-season-opponent is small for ranking suppressors among many candidates, so the stability test will be underpowered unless cells are pooled or shrunk.
Selecting each star's top suppressor on the same data used to judge stability will inflate apparent stability and premium size.
The reliability of play-type and defender-matchup premiums at this cell size has not been established in any retrieved record.
Many star-defender-opponent combinations will have few possessions, so a top suppressor may rest on very few sequences.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work covered nearby questions (play-type recommendation hit rates, counter stability across levels, regular-season proxy tests and single-game decision trees), but none tested suppressor identity across seasons or teammate X->Y premiums. The earlier results were artifact, inconclusive or untestable, which limits their weight on this question.

risks.text: Top-suppressor selection from many candidates will overstate both premium size and cross-season stability unless selection and evaluation are separated.
n=20 per cell gives low power to separate true suppression from noise, especially for negative teammate premiums.
Searching all teammate X->Y pairs for large negative premiums will produce many false positives without correction.
Suppression premium reliability at this sample size is unknown and must be measured before stability claims are interpreted.
Using full-season or future data to choose the suppressor, as in earlier records, would leak outcome information into the selection.
Opponent quality, teammate usage, lineup and pace can drive the apparent premium independently of the defender.
Roster, role and coaching changes across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons can break stability in ways unrelated to individual suppression.
Many star-defender-opponent cells will have few sequences, so top-suppressor identities may rest on very few observations.
Without a shuffled or placebo baseline, a stable-looking top suppressor may simply reflect persistent usage patterns.

design.estimand: Season-to-season reliability (intraclass correlation) of each star's defender-level suppression premium, and the rank stability of the top suppressor, with a shrunken estimate of teammate X->Y premium distribution compared against a permutation null.
design.unit: Player-season-opponent cell, with possession sequences as the within-cell observations. Premiums are estimated per defender and per teammate X->Y sequence.
design.sample: Regular-season NBA play-by-play for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 as the discovery and validation seasons, with 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) as the held-out season. Playoffs are excluded from the primary test. Only cells with a minimum pre-registered possession count are included.
design.power: Pre-registered minimum of cell size and simulated power before analysis. Stability is tested by simulation under the observed cell-size distribution; if power to detect a moderate reliability (for example ICC of 0.3) is below 0.8, the claim is reported as not testable at this size.
design.controls: Opponent quality, teammate usage rate, lineup and pace, and the defender's own minutes. Premiums are shrunk toward the league mean using empirical Bayes. Roster and role changes are flagged and excluded or stratified.
design.falsification: The stability claim is falsified if the cross-season ICC of the top-suppressor premium is not distinguishable from the permutation-null ICC, or if the top suppressor in the held-out season is no more likely than chance to match the top suppressor in the discovery seasons. The large negative teammate premium claim is falsified if no X->Y premium survives shrinkage and FDR control against the permutation null.
design.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across all teammate X->Y pairs and defenders, with the number of tests fixed before analysis. Selection of the top suppressor uses only discovery seasons; evaluation is on the held-out season.
design.decision_rule: Claim cross-season suppressor stability only if held-out ICC exceeds the permutation null at FDR 0.05 and the held-out top suppressor matches the discovery top suppressor more often than chance. Claim a negative teammate premium only if it survives shrinkage and FDR control and replicates in the held-out season. Otherwise report as uncertain or untestable. Do not issue best or avoid counter recommendations from these results.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, with 2025-26 used only as held-out and only after it is complete (from 2026-04-13). Play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters and defensive matchup files are version-locked at the analysis date; graph-derived play-type records are rebuilt from the same snapshot.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Each star's top sequential suppressor is stable across seasons, and some teammate X->Y sequences have large negative premiums.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=20 per player-season-opp; n=20

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
